M.name: Manual
M.desc: Performed and owned entirely by a named person. AI is not used to produce the output.

AG.name: AI-Generated
AG.desc: AI produces the draft from approved inputs and the Context Pack. A named person must validate it before it is used. It is never a deliverable as generated.

AA.name: AI-Assisted
AA.desc: A person produces the output. AI is used only to summarise, search, scan or suggest. The person decides.

AU.name: Automated
AU.desc: Deterministic tooling with no AI judgement: Jenkins pipeline, PMD, Sonar, OpenAPI diff, link-check jobs.

NA.name: AI Not Permitted
NA.desc: AI must not be used for this activity under any circumstances.

NF.name: New Application / New Feature
NF.when: A capability that does not exist today: a new application, module, screen set, service or integration.
examples: Mobile RFID scanning for physical asset verification
New integration with the ERP general ledger

CR.name: Enhancement / Change Request
CR.when: A change to behaviour, rules, screens, reports or interfaces that already exist and are baselined.
examples: Pro-rata daily depreciation for mid-year additions
Add cost-centre filter to the asset register report

SR.name: Issue Fix / Service Request
SR.when: Something is broken (defect), or an operational request that changes data, configuration or access rather than designed behaviour.
examples: Depreciation run posts duplicate entries for transferred assets (defect)
Correct useful life for 42 assets (data SR)
Add a role to a user group (access SR)

severity: Production down, financial misstatement (e.g. wrong depreciation posted to ledger), data loss or security breach
AI-X for RCA and fix. AI-A only to summarise logs.
Major function impaired; workaround is costly or risky
AI-X for RCA and fix. AI-A only to summarise logs.
RCA manual. Fix AI-G permitted after RCA approval.
RCA manual (short form). Fix AI-G permitted.
srTypes: Fix asset master records, re-run depreciation for a period, correct location or custodian
Scripted, reversible, before/after evidence. Scripts that change cost, accumulated depreciation or NBV are AI-X; other scripts AI-G with peer review and dry run.
Asset class useful life, depreciation rate table, label template, approval limits
Change record with old and new values; peer review; verification in test first. AI-A only.
Add or remove users, roles, location access
Approved by data owner; executed by admin; AI-X.
If code changes: re-route as a CR. If configuration only: change record and verification.
Upload template validation; sample verification of 10% or 20 rows, whichever is greater. AI-A for validation summaries.
techniques: Map every output item to a source item, and every source item to an output item. Unmapped output is removed; unmapped source is added.
The stage prompt requires AI to list every assumption and open question. The reviewer resolves each one; an unresolved item blocks the gate.
Every field, validation ID, error code, class, style class and API named by AI is looked up in the data dictionary or Context Pack registry.
Compare counts in and out: statements to REQs, dictionary columns to fields, REQs to test cases, approved cases to executed cases, scope to release notes.
Compare the output with the CP-99 reference artifact for the same surface: same sections, same patterns, same naming.
Lint, PMD, Checkstyle, Sonar, OpenAPI diff, SQL lint, secret scan, ID link check. Objective and blocking.
Wrong domain logic that looks right
A domain SME calculates sample values without looking at the AI output (for example WDV for a mid-year addition) and compares.
Tests are executed and results attached. Defect fixes show fail-before and pass-after. Automation is proven by a deliberate-fail check.
The author explains any AI-generated element on request. If it cannot be explained it is reworked, however plausible it looks.
For critical artifacts only: regenerate once from the same input. Material differences mean the input is ambiguous; fix the input, not the output.
universalChecklist: Generated from an approved, versioned input; input ID and version recorded
Standard stage prompt template used; Context Pack version recorded
AI Usage Declaration (T11) completed: tool, prompt template, sections generated
Assumption list present, and every assumption resolved by a person
Every output item traces to a source item; no orphan content
No invented identifiers: fields, validation IDs, error codes, APIs, classes, style classes
Reuse verified: every referenced component exists and is actually used
Structure follows the template; naming follows CP-11
Domain rules spot-checked by independent re-derivation where financial values are involved
No personal data, production data or secrets in the prompt or the output
Reviewer is not the AI operator; sign-off recorded in T10
idConventions: FAM asset master · DEP depreciation · LBL labelling and tracking · AUD validation and audit · PLT platform
<MOD>-REQ-<nnn>; a revised requirement keeps its ID with .r<n>
[DEP-REQ-214] Apply daily pro-rata to WDV additions
contextPack: Root instruction file loaded by every AI tool; points to /ai-context and states the binding rules
Modules, surfaces, module prefixes, domain glossary (asset class, SLM, WDV, CWIP, NBV, impairment, label)
Layering, exceptions, logging, transactions, audit trail, versioning policy
Packages, classes, methods, tables, columns, API paths, events, branches, commits, test IDs
Canonical project skeleton per surface and where each kind of file goes
Every base class, utility, validator and component, with when to use it and the do-not-rewrite list
Any shared code added or retired
Design tokens, approved style classes, component catalogue for web and mobile
REST conventions, versioning, pagination, error envelope, event naming
Every validation ID and error code with message text; the only source for SFVD and code
Test case template, ID convention, negative-pattern library, automation and locator patterns, device matrix
Seed data structure, standard asset fixtures, masking rules, data builders
Authorisation model, PII handling, audit log rules, secrets policy, AI data rules
One approved prompt per stage, S0 to S9
The gate checklists from T10, so AI can self-check before a human reviews
One reference feature per surface (service, mobile, internal web) for AI to imitate
principles: AI drafts, a person decides, the gate records.
AI output is never a deliverable as generated. It becomes one only when a named reviewer accepts it and the gate is recorded in T10.
Standards, structure, shared libraries, style classes, registries and test data live in one versioned Context Pack that every prompt loads.
Every artifact, commit, test case and defect carries its requirement, CR or SR ID. If it is not linked it does not ship.
A new utility, base method, style class, validation ID or service is justified in writing, or it is not created.
Evidence or it did not happen.
A gate passes only with a recorded artifact: checklist, scan result, approval. Verbal sign-off is not a gate.

stages.name: Intake and Classification
stages.purpose: Register every new work item, classify it as a New Feature, Change Request or Issue / Service Request, link it to the current baseline, and route it to the correct process path.
entry: Work item raised in Jira by business, support or an internal team

inputs.item: Current baseline: RTM, SFVD versions, release history

activities.activity: Log the item with requester, module, surface(s) and business priority
Summarise long descriptions, e-mail threads and logs into a structured intake summary
Search the RTM and backlog for duplicates and related items
Classify the work type (NF / CR / SR); assign ID and module prefix
For issues: set provisional severity P1 to P4
Assign the accountable owner and process path; record Gate G0

outputs.output: Classified Jira item: work type, ID, module, severity

checklist: Work type classified using the rules in section 3.4; borderline cases decided by the Architect
Intake summary reflects the original request: nothing added, nothing lost
Duplicates and related items confirmed by a person, not accepted from the AI suggestion
Module prefix, surface(s) and requester recorded
Severity set for issues (P1 to P4) with a one-line justification
Accountable owner and process path assigned
stages.gateText: G0 Intake approved: item classified, ID assigned, owner named, process path selected.
stages.aiRule: AI may summarise and search. AI must not classify the work type or set severity.
automatedChecks: Jira mandatory-field validation (work type, module, requester)

stages.name: Requirements and Review Points
stages.purpose: Turn the business need into an approved, uniquely identified requirement register with acceptance criteria. This register is the root of all traceability.
entry: G0 passed; work type NF, or CR after impact analysis (T04)

inputs.item: Business requirement note and client review points
Current workflow, screen inventory and report list
Domain glossary: asset classes, SLM / WDV, useful life, CWIP, impairment, disposal, label formats
Context Pack sections CP-00, CP-40 and stage prompt P-S1

activities.activity: Prepare the business requirement note with review points
Generate the draft register: one ID per requirement, acceptance criteria, impact map, assumptions and open questions
Reconcile the register with the source: every statement mapped, nothing invented
Walk through open questions with the business and record answers
Verify domain and statutory rules (depreciation, capitalisation thresholds, audit retention)
Approve the register, freeze REQ-IDs and create RTM rows

outputs.output: Requirement Register v1.0 with REQ-IDs and acceptance criteria
Assumption and open-question log, fully resolved
Impact map across microservices, mobile and internal web

checklist: Every statement in the source note maps to at least one REQ-ID
No requirement exists without a source statement (nothing invented by AI)
Each requirement is atomic, testable and has acceptance criteria
Every AI-declared assumption and open question is answered by the business, not by AI
Depreciation, capitalisation and statutory rules verified by a domain SME
Impact on microservices, mobile and internal web identified
Non-functional needs captured: volume, response time, retention, security
REQ-IDs follow the convention and are unique in the RTM
AI Usage Declaration (T11) attached with the Context Pack version
stages.gateText: G1 Requirements approved: register v1.0 signed by the Product Owner, REQ-IDs frozen, RTM rows created.
stages.aiRule: AI may structure, de-duplicate and draft acceptance criteria. AI must not answer its own open questions or decide scope.
automatedChecks: REQ-ID format and uniqueness check in the RTM

stages.name: SFVD: Screens, Fields, Validations
stages.purpose: Specify every screen, field, validation, error message and business flow precisely enough that development and testing work from the same truth.

inputs.item: SFVD template and two approved SFVDs as worked examples
Data dictionary and entity relationship model
UI style guide and component catalogue

activities.activity: Generate the SFVD draft per screen: purpose, actors, flow, field table, validations, error codes, user stories, UI references
Verify field by field against the data dictionary
Verify every validation ID and error code exists in the registry; raise a registry change for genuinely new ones
Verify reuse call-outs: the named components and validators exist and fit
Business walkthrough of flows and screens
Baseline the SFVD; update the requirement-screen-field matrix; release to Dev and QA the same day

checklist: Every screen and field maps to a REQ-ID
Every field matches the data dictionary: name, type, length, mandatory
Every validation ID and error code exists in the registry; none invented
Business flows match the approved register, including negative and exception flows
UI references use only approved style classes and components
Reuse call-outs verified against the shared library index
Mobile offline behaviour stated where applicable
Audit-trail fields and role permissions specified for every screen
AI assumption list resolved; AI Usage Declaration attached
stages.gateText: G2 SFVD baselined: matrix updated, document released to Development and QA on the same day.
stages.aiRule: AI may draft. AI must not create new fields, validation IDs, error codes or style classes.
automatedChecks: Registry lookup script for validation and error IDs (manual lookup until scripted)

stages.name: Solution Design and Interface Contract
stages.purpose: Decide how the change is built across services and surfaces, and agree the API contract before any code is written.
entry: For CR and SR: only when the impact analysis or RCA shows a contract, schema or cross-service change

inputs.item: Service map, bounded contexts and event topics

activities.activity: Generate the design draft: service impact, OpenAPI contract, DTO and entity design, sequence diagrams, migration draft, reuse plan
Run OpenAPI lint and diff, and SQL migration lint
Architecture review: boundaries, reuse, backward compatibility, versioning
Database review: indexes, migration, rollback
Security review: authorisation, PII, audit fields
Merge the contract to the contract repository; record the design decision

checklist: No cross-service database access; bounded contexts respected
Contract backward compatible, or the version bumped with consumers listed
The capability does not already exist in another service
Base classes and shared libraries reused; no parallel utilities designed
Error envelope, pagination and naming follow CP-22
Mobile offline and synchronisation impact addressed
Migration reversible; rollback script present and reviewed by the DBA
Authorisation, audit fields and PII handling reviewed by Security
Design decision and the alternatives considered are recorded
stages.gateText: G3 Design approved: contract merged to the contract repository before coding starts.
stages.aiRule: AI may draft designs and contracts. AI must not merge a contract or approve a breaking change.
automatedChecks: OpenAPI diff against the previous version

stages.name: Development
stages.purpose: Implement the approved design inside the existing structure, reusing shared code, with unit tests.
entry: G3 passed, or G1 / RCA approval for a change without design impact
Task carries a REQ-ID or defect ID

inputs.item: SFVD section, API contract and design note
Coding standards, naming conventions, folder structure
Shared library index and UI style guide
Golden reference example for the surface

activities.activity: Create the branch named with the ID
Generate code inside the existing structure, unit tests, configuration, i18n keys and migration
Search the shared library before accepting any new class, utility or CSS
Run the local build, unit tests, PMD and Sonar scan
Self-review against the T09 checklist; remove unused and alternative code
Raise a pull request of 400 lines or fewer with T09 and the AI Usage Declaration

outputs.output: AI Usage Declaration in the pull request

checklist: Shared library searched; no duplicate utility, validator, base method or CSS created
Package, class, method and file names follow CP-11
Layering and folder placement follow CP-12
No hardcoded values, credentials or environment-specific configuration
Exception handling, logging and audit trail follow CP-10
Queries checked for N+1, pagination and index use
Unit tests cover new logic, including boundary and negative cases
No unused or commented-out AI-generated alternatives remain
Branch name and every commit carry the REQ-ID or defect ID
Pull request 400 lines or fewer, or split; T09 completed
The developer can explain every line
stages.gateText: G4 Pull request ready: CI green, checklist complete, AI usage declared.
stages.aiRule: AI may generate code and tests. For P1 and P2 defects AI is not permitted (see section 5.3).

stages.name: Code Review
stages.purpose: Independent human verification that the code is correct, consistent, reusable and secure before it is merged.

inputs.item: Pull request diff and T09 checklist

activities.activity: Generate a review aid: diff summary, standards-deviation scan, duplicate detection, missing-test hints
Confirm the CI quality gate result
Review business logic against the SFVD line by line
Check reuse, layering, naming and contract adherence
Security and data-access review (Security consulted for sensitive changes)
Approve or request changes; record the decision

outputs.output: Approved pull request or review comments
Merge with REQ-ID in the message

checklist: Reviewer is not the developer who ran the AI prompt
Business logic matches the SFVD and acceptance criteria
Reuse opportunities enforced, not merely noted
Contract adherence and backward compatibility confirmed
Security, authorisation, input validation and PII handling checked
Tests are meaningful: they assert behaviour and include negative cases
Sonar: zero blocker and critical issues; duplication and coverage within thresholds
All review comments resolved; nothing the reviewer cannot explain is merged
stages.gateText: G5 Code approved and merged by an independent reviewer.
stages.aiRule: AI may assist the reviewer. AI never approves or merges.

stages.name: Test Design
stages.purpose: Derive complete test cases and test data from the baselined SFVD and contract, in parallel with design and development.
entry: G2 passed (and G3 for contract-based cases)

inputs.item: Test case template and ID convention
Test data and seed data specification
Boundary and negative scenario pattern library
Index of the existing regression suite

activities.activity: Generate test cases: functional, validation, UI, flow, integration, cross-surface; positive and negative; expected results; REQ mapping; automation flag
Generate test data requirements mapped to the seed structure
Coverage reconciliation: every REQ-ID and every field validation covered
Remove duplicates of existing regression cases
Verify expected results against the SFVD; SME re-calculates financial values
Approve the suite; baseline it in the test management tool; update the RTM

checklist: Every REQ-ID has at least one positive and one negative case
Every field validation in the SFVD has a test case
Expected results traced to SFVD text, not inferred
Depreciation, label and audit expected values independently re-calculated by the SME
No duplicate of an existing regression case
Test data follows the seed structure; personal and financial data masked
Priority, regression and automation tags set
Device, browser and role coverage matches the matrix
stages.gateText: G6 Test suite approved and baselined in the test management tool.
stages.aiRule: AI may draft cases and data. AI must not decide expected results for financial calculations without SME verification.
automatedChecks: RTM coverage check: REQ-IDs without a test case are flagged

stages.name: Test Execution and Automation
stages.purpose: Execute the approved suite, automate the agreed cases, and prove that nothing was silently dropped.
entry: Build deployed to the test environment

inputs.item: Automation framework patterns and locator standard

activities.activity: Load seed data
Generate automation scripts: page objects, locators, data-driven steps
Review scripts one-to-one against approved cases; verify assertions
Execute manual and automated tests
Draft defect reports from failures
Run the automation parity check; record deferrals with reasons

outputs.output: Automated scripts added to the regression pack

checklist: Every automated script maps one-to-one to an approved case; no steps dropped
Assertions verify expected results, proven by a deliberate-fail check on a sample
No hardcoded data, fixed waits or environment coupling
Scripts are independent and repeatable in any order
Parity: approved = executed + automated + formally deferred
Every failure has a defect linked to its REQ-ID
Deferred cases have a reason, an owner and a target release
stages.gateText: G7 Test exit: parity 100%, no open P1 or P2 defects, evidence attached.
stages.aiRule: AI may draft scripts and defect descriptions. AI must not mark a test as passed.
automatedChecks: Parity check: approved = executed + automated + formally deferred

stages.name: Build and Release
stages.purpose: Produce a signed, immutable and traceable release package.

inputs.item: Merged code and the release scope from Jira

activities.activity: Build the immutable artifact with a version tag
Generate release notes from commits and REQ-IDs, config diff summary and rollback steps
Reconcile release notes with the RTM and Jira scope
Verify configuration differences for each environment
Migration dry run on a production-like copy
Record release approval

checklist: Version number unique and follows policy; artifact checksum recorded
Every release-note line traces to a merged pull request and REQ-ID; nothing omitted
Known issues and deferred cases listed
Configuration differences verified for each environment; no secrets in notes
Migration dry run passed; rollback tested
Open defects accepted or deferred in writing
Release approval recorded before promotion
stages.gateText: G8 Release approved: signed package, RTM snapshot attached.
stages.aiRule: AI may draft notes and runbooks. AI must not trigger a build promotion.
automatedChecks: RTM link check: every REQ in scope has passed tests

stages.name: Deploy, Verify and Close
stages.purpose: Deploy safely, prove it works in production, and close the loop with a frozen audit baseline.

activities.activity: Pre-deployment validation and backup confirmation
Deploy through the Jenkins pipeline following the runbook
Execute the smoke pack
Summarise post-deployment logs and metrics for anomalies
Monitor for the agreed window; decide go or rollback
Business sign-off; freeze the RTM; close Jira items; raise context-gap changes

checklist: Backup confirmed by a named person before deployment
Deployment executed from the runbook; deviations recorded
Smoke pack 100% passed, executed by QA rather than the deployer
Monitoring window completed with no unexplained errors
Rollback decision owner named before deployment started
Business sign-off recorded
RTM frozen and versioned with the release
Lessons learned captured; context gaps raised on T14
stages.gateText: G9 Release closed: smoke passed, monitoring clean, RTM frozen.
stages.aiRule: AI may summarise logs. AI must not execute deployment or rollback actions.

S1: Every impacted REQ-ID confirmed by the Architect, not only suggested by AI
Contract and schema impact assessed; Minor or Major classification justified
Regression selection confirmed by the QA Lead and includes the critical-path pack
Financial rule changes: prospective or retrospective decided; Finance approval recorded
Effort and schedule agreed with the Product Owner

S0: Issue reproduced, or request validated, before any change
Classification and severity justified; re-routed if code or new behaviour is needed
Script is reversible and the rollback script was tested
Scripts changing financial values were written manually and reviewed by two people
Dry run on a production-like copy; before and after evidence attached
Executed by an authorised admin under a change record

The five whys reach a process cause, not only a code cause
The gate that missed the defect is named, with evidence
Failing test committed before the fix
Preventive action for the missed gate assigned with an owner and date
Data impact assessed; correction raised as an SR if needed
P1 / P2: reviewed by the Architect

Classification and severity justified; re-routed if code or new behaviour is needed
